eventDefinition: An 'event year' is a year in the top quarter of the region's own event record (highEventYears in hazards/zones.json): GDACS floods, NASA Global Landslide Catalog, FIRMS MODIS fire detections or IBTrACS cyclones.

anomalyDetectionAccuracy.definition: For each cutoff year Y, the class computed with only baseline years before Y is compared with the class from the complete 1991–2020 (daily: 1997–2020) baseline. Years from 2021 are excluded because both baselines are then identical. Years before the baseline reached 20 values are not computable.

falseAlarmRate.definition: Flagged (watch or warning) seasons that were not event years, as a share of all flagged seasons, pooled over hazard regions. Same-season matching replaces the 30-day window because the inputs are seasonal.

missedEvents.definition: Event years with no watch or warning in the same season, as a share of all event years, pooled over hazard regions.

leadTime.reason: Not computable: seasonal screening is only possible after the season has ended and been published, so it cannot precede an event inside that season. Lead time needs daily or monthly inputs (intelligence.py --refresh).

confidenceCalibration.definition: Share of real-time anomaly assessments, per anomaly-confidence grade, whose class matched the full-record class.

geographicCoverage.definition: Share of study-area land cells with at least 20 baseline values and a value in the latest year, per variable and season.

limitations: Event records are uneven: news-based landslide reports under-count remote areas, GDACS coverage improved over time, and MODIS overpass times drifted after about 2020.
The wildfire backtest does not require a linked driver, because the link itself is estimated from the full record.
Hazard regions are approximate boxes; countries and cities are not backtested separately.
